phase: Unity U4C3 — topology-safe / manifold Surface Nets
question: Can scalar-topology patch identity repair the two deterministic fine-tier Surface Nets nonmanifold edges while preserving the U3-selected renderer, exact U4C2 fields, visual character, and deterministic brick stitching?
rootCause: One vertex per active cell collapsed disconnected boundary surface patches; four distinct primal crossing-edge quads reused the same dual edge, producing exactly one four-use edge in each known case.

fix.faceConnectivity: Crossing-edge graph over the six cube faces; two-crossing faces connect directly; checkerboard faces use the bilinear saddle/asymptotic decider with deterministic positive-solid near-tie policy.
fix.vertexIdentity: Global cell address plus a 12-bit crossing-edge component mask.
fix.faceEmission: Each incident cell selects the vertex component containing the emitted primal crossing edge.
fix.vertexPlacement: Hermite crossings, normal and material weights are accumulated per patch.

performance.editorMatrixObservation: One warm run, not a median or production budget. A/0.25 m: 104.8258 ms vs 147.1634 ms baseline; B/0.0625 m: 915.2180 ms vs 961.8102 ms; C/0.125 m: 239.3140 ms vs 333.7708 ms.

findings: Named opposite-corner regression exposes the unsupported interior-connectivity class without requiring MC33 for B/C.
Recorded B/C repairs, 12 matrix rows, seam, stress tests, visual comparisons and final Player evidence are credible.
No remaining technical blocker; arbitrary trilinear topology and higher-genus surfaces remain outside this qualification.
